newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Gore will meet Hong Kong's Lee next week.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Gore will meet Hong Kong's Lee next week.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore will meet Martin Lee, the leader of Hong Kong's democracy movement, a White House official said on Saturday.

Lee is on a lobbying mission in the United States ahead of the switch of Hong Kong from British rule to Chinese control on July 1, amid concern over indications that China wants to tighten controls on political and civil liberties.

"Sometime next week the vice president will meet with Mr. Lee and he'll see the president as well. The president will join the meeting," said the White House official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

U.S. officials said on Friday that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will meet Lee on Monday. They also said she was considering a joint British-Chinese invitation to attend the festivities when the British colony is returned to Chinese rule.

In the meeting with Lee, Albright will discuss issues related to Hong Kong's reversion to China's control, including protection of civil liberties and fundamental freedoms of the rule of law, "which are very important," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
